subject.title: [Feature]: Silent reasoning — exclude thinking content from session transcript

question: Should OpenClaw add a core transcript-persistence policy that lets reasoning run while excluding thinking blocks from durable and transcript-facing history, and what provider replay state must remain private to the runtime?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses config/API, durable storage, provider replay, ACP/session APIs, compaction, memory, and docs, so a one-site implementation would create competing semantics without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Design a core persistence policy
options.body: Add an explicit core policy that separates reasoning production, display visibility, durable transcript storage, and provider-private replay state.

options.title: Keep this as plugin workaround only
options.body: Document before_message_write as the supported local workaround, accepting that built-in session APIs and memory consumers keep current semantics.

options.title: Defer beyond replay hardening
options.body: Keep current provider replay sanitizers and close or pause this feature until maintainers decide silent durable transcripts are product scope.

recommendation.title: Design a core persistence policy
recommendation.body: Add an explicit core policy that separates reasoning production, display visibility, durable transcript storage, and provider-private replay state.

likelyOwner.reason: The current transcript append, replay-history, and reasoning-normalization surfaces route most directly through Peter Steinberger's recent main history.
